payload.name: Preserve Explicit Role and Trait Attributions
payload.description: When extracting a memory from a message where a speaker explicitly states another person's role or qualities, capture the specific attribution instead of reducing it to generic encouragement.
content: During extraction, if a source message contains an explicit statement about a person's role, title, or qualities (e.g., 'you are a perfect mentor', 'your positivity and determination will make it a hit'), create or update a memory candidate that records that specific claim, including the exact trait words used, and do not replace it with a vague paraphrase such as 'encourages' or 'believes in potential'.

When the same message also contains separate encouragement or support, keep the explicit attribution as its own memory candidate or as an explicit, retained part of the candidate content so the fact remains directly answerable later.

solves: The diagnosed cause is that an extraction candidate paraphrased an explicit role and trait attribution (being a perfect mentor, having positivity and determination) into generic encouragement, making the fact unanswerable later. This rule addresses any future message where a speaker explicitly attributes a role, title, or personal quality to someone; the reusable failure mechanism is replacing specific claims with vague supportive summaries. It applies during candidate extraction in Construction and prevents the loss of answerable facts before CRUD decisions.
